name: Moththwack
description: Open the exchange with a straight thrust while the other blade keeps its guard hook ready.

name: Levering Shearing
description: Drag the heel of the guard hook down the opposing blade to pull the weapon out of line.

name: Pleatprop
description: Pin the elbow to the ribs and let the blade lie along the forearm to stop a cut.

name: Scutecurl
description: Advance in a straight line with both blades level so every step also threatens a thrust.

name: Viselike Flurry
description: Wedge the guard hook behind an opposing blade and wrench it away with a quick qi pulse in the wrist.

name: Brisk Shearedge
description: While one blade holds the opposing steel hooked the other drives a qi-sharpened thrust through the opening.

name: Rugged Clipper
description: Bring both edges together across the target like the blades of a pair of shears.

name: Hiltfold Carapace
description: Hold the blades apart in a V that catches a blow in the notch between them.

name: Brisk Wristside
description: Snip across the opponent's wrist with a swift closing of the blades to make the grip fail.

name: Pirouetting Platepoint
description: Close the shear and step back in the same breath so the counter finds only air.

name: Savage Cheekhilt
description: Catch a shaft in the open V and close the blades to bite deep into the wood.

name: Fierce Edgepair
description: Qi runs to both edges at the instant of closing and the shear cuts through leather and light mail.

name: Padded Doublehilt
description: Turn the shear into a ward by catching a blade in the V and twisting it from its owner's hand.

name: Resolute Fliptang
description: Move the lead blade in a steady orbit in front of the body so thrusts are swept outward.

name: Pleatbarrier
description: The second blade circles the opposite way so that the two rings together cover high and low.

name: Acrid Crossing
description: Break out of the circle with a sudden jab through the gap the turning blades just made.

name: Clutching Shortedge
description: Spin both blades with a loose wrist until the opponent cannot tell which will strike.

name: Scudding Shortedge
description: Move around the opponent on a small circle with the blades turning in time with the feet.

name: Wingswat
description: Let the orbiting blade finish its arc in a cut across the opponent's exposed forearm.

name: Stalwart Swingguard
description: Spread qi along the whole path of the circling blades so the orbit becomes a thin barrier.

name: Brutal Doublehilt
description: Turn the outgoing circle into a qi-backed cut that lands the moment a blow has been swept aside.

name: Pleatswat
description: Drive the elbow forward so the short cut that follows lands with the weight of the whole arm.

name: Wingbarrier
description: Raise the knuckle guard to meet a strike on the hardest edge of the weapon.

name: Doughty Fliptang
description: Jab at one spot twice in a row so the second thrust passes where the first made the cloth give.

name: Pleatcurl
description: Drift in sideways steps at chest distance so every opening stays within reach of a short blade.

name: Edgepair Slap
description: A pulse of qi in the wrist doubles the force of a chop thrown from only a hand's width away.

name: Mothprop
description: A qi pulse in the elbow forces the opponent's blade arm outward and leaves the ribs open.

name: Levering Wristside
description: Catch the opposing blade where the two swords cross and hold it in the crook.

name: Flurrybarrier
description: Slide the guard under the opponent's hilt and lift to pry the weapon hand upward.

name: Keen Scissor
description: While one blade pins the opposing weapon the other chops at the exposed wrist or elbow.

name: Lithe Scissor
description: When a lock begins to give step out and let the bound blades fall away together.

name: Burdening Snapcut
description: Hold the opposing sword between both blades and keep it still against any attempt to wrest free.

name: Wingscreen
description: Set the pinned weapon between your face and the foe's second hand so it cannot strike over it.

name: Stalling Flurry
description: Send qi into the crossed blades so the lock tightens and the opposing steel grates and stalls.

name: Clutching Cheekhilt
description: Turn the locked blades a quarter circle like a key and tear the opponent's grip open.

name: Rugged Swingguard
description: Burst out of a bind with a qi-driven double cut that finishes before the opponent resets.

name: Clay Crossing
description: Begin the exchange by cutting across the opponent's line and letting the blades meet in an X.

name: Regimen Hiltfold
description: Keep the crossing of the blades at the center of the body and hold it against pressure.

name: Shearedge Flog
description: Take the high blow on the crossed steel while the lower blade slices at the opponent's thigh.

name: Veering Shearing
description: Step off the crossing line to the outside so the foe's momentum carries it past.

name: Humwing
description: Form a second crossing over the first to stop a follow-up cut that came behind the first.

name: Harsh Clipper
description: Qi flares along the crossing as the blades part and both edges cut outward at once.

name: Lunarpleat
description: Meet a blow at the crossing and return a share of its force along the opposing blade.

name: Honedscute
description: Cut left then right in an even beat that never leaves one side of the body bare.

name: Haze Cheekhilt
description: Lift both blades like raised wings to turn a strike from above toward either shoulder.

name: Doughty Edgepair
description: Jolt the pommel into the opponent's ribs when the cut has been caught.

name: Ducking Wristside
description: Roll the weight from foot to foot in a sideways pace that keeps the blades facing front.

name: Buttressed Doublehilt
description: Parry with one blade and return the cut with the other in the same turn of the wrist.

name: Slumber Snapcut
description: Let a blade sag as if tired and cut upward the moment the opponent steps in.

name: Crossing Thwack
description: Send the point through a gap barely wider than the blade and into the gap's far side.

name: Brassflurry
description: A single qi-fed cut that ends the long course's opening drills with the breath fully behind the edge.

name: Haze Platepoint
description: Weave both blades in a flowing figure while qi guides each wrist to meet blows before they land.

name: Woven Hiltfold
description: Chain thrust cut and hook in one unbroken rush with qi renewing itself at every change of hand.

name: Pleatswerve
description: Duck beneath a spear shaft as it sweeps and come up on the inside of the point.

name: Winghasp
description: Ride the flat of one blade along a spear's shaft toward the hands that hold it.

name: Brawn Platepoint
description: Cut the hand that grips the shaft before the owner can draw back to a longer reach.

name: Humscute
description: Parry the point wide with the near blade and press close before the shaft can swing again.

name: Shearedge Barrier
description: Pin the shaft against the opponent's body with both guards and a pulse of qi that locks their arms.

name: Gleamwing
description: Once inside the long weapon's reach drive a qi-sharpened point through the gap beneath the arm.

name: Snapcut Swat
description: As one blade turns a blow the other is already cutting back along the same path.

name: Mothbuckle
description: Parry toward the centerline and answer straight away with a thrust past the opponent's shoulder.

name: Hum Swingguard
description: Parry toward the outside and answer with a hooking cut to the exposed back of the arm.

name: Stalwart Fliptang
description: Stand with the blades low and loose and let the opponent commit to the first stroke.

name: Springing Shearing
description: Step back with the turn of the parry so the answering cut lands at its full reach.

name: Stalling Shortedge
description: Tap the opposing blade on its offbeat to throw the timing of the next stroke.

name: Ember Flurry
description: Gather the energy of the parry into a qi-backed counterstroke thrown from the same wrist.

name: Gleam Shearedge
description: Receive the incoming cut on the blade and send a measured share of its force back along the line.
